messages:
Evan Park: Quick RFC follow-up: proposal to treat Canary/A-B signals as first-class contracts so the rollout actuator can remain dumb and auditable. Thoughts?
Nina Lopez: Interesting. By "signal contract" you mean a typed envelope with semantic keys rather than ad-hoc metrics?
Evan Park: Exactly. Envelope carries channels (latency, correctness, infra), a severity level, a provenance tag, and an expiry. Actuator only reads envelope and enforces policy rules.
Diego Ramos: That reduces coupling. Two questions: who owns combiners (merge multiple signals) and how do we prevent noisy signals from causing oscillations?
Evan Park: Ownership: combiners live in "signal providers" behind a feature-flag. We'll ship a central combiner and allow local lightweight combiners for emergency heuristics. Oscillation: policy includes a damping token bucket and a min-stable-window.
Priya Shah: Need explicit safety budget per-service. Example: max_auto_rollbacks_per_day and a cumulative error-exposure budget. If budget exhausted -> manual-only.
Tom Baker: From infra side, we want signals that are robust to sampling variance. Recommend standard buckets (p50/p95/p99) and a min-sample threshold before emitting a high-severity signal.
Nina Lopez: UX note: operators want a concise reason string plus links to the raw evidence. Suggest `evidence_url` and a short human summary in the envelope.
Evan Park: Agreed. Proposed envelope proto (informal):
```
envelope:
  channel: latency|quality|infra
  level: info|warn|critical
  score: 0-100
  reason: short-text
  evidence_url: https://...
  expires_at: 2026-03-21T18:06:30Z
  provenance: ["latency-evaluator:v1","sampler:region-east-2"]
```
Diego Ramos: How should actuators translate level/score to actions? Simple mapping table? e.g., score>80 && level==critical -> divert 100% of cohort; score 40-80 -> reduce weight by 50%.
Priya Shah: Let's avoid hardcoded numbers in code. Policy config stored per-service with defaults and operator-overrides. Also add a backoff multiplier to the mapping so repeated signals soften over time.
Tom Baker: For speed, local actuators should cache the latest policy and envelopes with TTL and apply immediately. But they must accept signed envelopes to avoid replay attacks.
Nina Lopez: Signed envelopes + monotonic sequence id prevents replay. Also include a small nonce for debug correlation.
Evan Park: Rollout orchestration: controllers emit cohort events -> signal evaluators subscribe, publish envelopes -> actuators apply mapping. Central combiner also writes to audit log.
Diego Ramos: Testing: we need a simulation harness that replays realistic traffic and injects signals to verify damping/backoff and budget behavior. I can spike a sim next sprint.
Priya Shah: Add circuit breaker: if actuator detects >N policy-driven changes in M minutes for same cohort, it should freeze auto actions, open a page to oncall, and escalate.
Tom Baker: Agree. Also add a 'graceful fallback' action set: observe|partial-divert|cohort-quarantine|rollback. Partial-divert supports fractional weights.
Nina Lopez: What about A-B experiments where we want to keep variant delta small? Envelope should support `impact_estimate` (expected delta on key metrics) so actuator can reason about safe step sizes.
Evan Park: Nice. Also, metadata requirement: service owner, rollout id, and experiment name in envelope for traceability.
Priya Shah: Logs: store envelope and raw metric slices for 90 days minimum. For privacy-sensitive customers, provide an opt-out with reduced retention but keep signalled decisions.
Diego Ramos: Migration plan: shadow signals for 2 weeks, then opt-in for low-risk services, then wider rollout. Provide a fallback flag to revert to legacy controller per-service.
Tom Baker: Implementation detail: use gRPC for envelope push with TLS+JWT; fallback to signed HTTP webhook for legacy infra.
Evan Park: I'll draft a concise appendix (schema, default mapping, policies) and link to this thread. Action items: Nina -> metric buckets doc, Diego -> sim harness, Priya -> safety-budget schema, Tom -> signed-envelope transport.
deploy-bot: deploy: canary started for recommendations v3 cohort=3% at 2026-03-21T17:18Z :rocket:
Evan Park: thanks all, I'll schedule a 30m sync to finalize defaults.
